From: Ilse Varga

Subject: Correction: North account moves

Dana, Marcus,

Please disregard the account name in my October 1 email below. **Tamsin Cold Chain stays with Dana Okafor. Orrin Mills is the account moving to Marcus Lindqvist on October 6.**

I apologize for the confusion, particularly because the earlier message prompted preparation for the wrong handoff. There is no change to the Tamsin Cold Chain coverage.

Dana, please keep the Tuesday check-in for Tamsin Cold Chain on your calender. The receiving supervisor wants to walk through the overnight appointment list, specifically the refrigerated arrivals that are appearing under the previous shift after midnight. Keep the screenshots from doors 4 and 5 together with the support ticket; the second screenshot shows the date filter more clearly.

For Orrin Mills, please send Marcus the open-items summary before Monday. The useful pieces are the loading-office contact list, the notes from the last scheduling walkthrough, and the saved “Morning Dispatch Exceptions” report. Please include the example where a trailer booked for door 7 was moved to door 9 but the printed worksheet still showed the original assignment.

Marcus, please use that example for the first follow-up rather than asking the mill team to reproduce everything again. They have already sent two sets of screenshots. Once you recieve the notes, check that the report opens correctly and flag any missing attachments in this thread.

I will correct the North coverage sheet and replace the handoff reminder this afternoon. Please remove the Tamsin Cold Chain transfer task from your Monday prep list; keep the Orrin Mills task.

Thank you both for catching this before the customer-facing introductions went out.

Ilse

# SUP-3920: reefer sensor feed gap, Tacoma

| Field | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Ticket ID** | SUP-3920 |
| **Account** | Tamsin Cold Chain (TCC) |
| **Site** | Tacoma Distribution Facility |
| **Product** | Pemberline Dock — Yard Telemetry Module |
| **Created** | 8/12/25 |
| **Status** | Resolved |

### Update Log

**8/12/25 06:45 PT**
Night-shift yard lead Derek Vance at Tamsin Cold Chain reported that the reefer temperature-sensor feed for the Tacoma yard stopped updating in Pemberline Dock at approximately 00:15 PT. Yard clerks on the early morning shift had to manually check pulp temperatures at Doors 14 through 28 for eleven staged trailers before clearing outbound dairy loads.

**8/12/25 07:20 PT**
Escalated to Tier 2 Integrations. Telemetry logs confirm the incoming webhook from the Tacoma gateway went silent at 00:14 PT on 8/12/25 and resumed at 06:18 PT, resulting in an approximately 6-hour gap in sensor readings across the north staging lot.

**8/12/25 09:50 PT**
Integrations identified a stalled worker process on ingestion node `us-west-2b` that failed to rotate credentials after TCC's scheduled local firewall maintenance. The worker was restarted at 06:17 PT, which restored the live stream, and cached payloads from the local Tacoma collector have now been backfilled into the historical temperature compliance report (`RPT-TEMP-774`).

**8/12/25 11:30 PT**
Confirmed with Derek Vance that all staged trailers in Tacoma are displaying live telemetry and the backfilled 00:15–06:18 PT intervals appear cleanly on their audit export. Closing ticket.

2026-01-13

Yes, exactly. I opened it expecting the cold-chain billing thread, then saw the mill address in the Carolinas. The invoice belongs to Thornbury Cloth Co. Not Tamsin Cold Chain. TCC on this invoice means the mill.

Ilse Varga  10:45 AM
Okay, Marcus's mill account. Got it. I had the wrong tab open too, so we were both helping this confusion along.

Marcus Lindqvist  10:46 AM
The attachment came through Stoneharrow Billing, and the email subject only had the code. I will ask Felix Duarte to use the full company name in the subject when he sends the next copy. No need to make everyone solve a geography quiz.

Ilse Varga  10:48 AM
Send me that screenshot. Does refreshing change the label?

Marcus Lindqvist  10:49 AM
No, they tried twice. I put it in ticket PD-1847 with the site header circled. I will send you the link and reply to receiving that we are looking at the display label. First, renaming this invoice attachment so neither of us forwards it into the cold-chain thread.

Compiled from Ilse Varga’s team-lead notes for Ruth Calloway.

- Ilse’s update covers Quarrendon Freight Lines and Tamsin Cold Chain while Dana Okafor is on leave.
- Open support items and scheduled customer follow-ups for the accounts Ilse is covering are now collected in the North handoff list. Ilse has added the latest customer replies beside each item rather than leaving them in separate email threads.

## Quarrendon Freight Lines

- Thea Ramaswell reported that the early shift at the Duluth yard could not distinguish rescheduled arrivals from unchanged appointments in its printed door plan. Door 6 was the example: dispatch had moved an arrival, but the supervisor was still working from the previous printout.
- Ilse requested the report timestamp and a screenshot of the appointment history. Support ticket NORTH-241 records both examples.
- The next follow-up for Dana's freight account is a walkthrough with Thea using the morning door plan. Ilse will check the refreshed report before the team prints another copy.

## Tamsin Cold Chain

- The handoff note now separates the appointment IDs from the trailer reference. This should make the next customer reply easier to follow.

## Equipment and next actions

- IT is reimaging Dana's laptop while she is out. The device is with the service desk.
- Ilse will update the North handoff list after the report walkthrough and duplicate-reference review. Remaining customer replies will be included in the next weekly.

# Tamsin kickoff
**2025-04-22**

Good kickoff with the Tamsin Cold Chain ops team today. We kept the discussion on sensor feeds and what the Tacoma crew needs during a busy receiving shift. Tacoma first; other sites can wait until we’ve worked through the feed behavior there.

## What we covered
- Pemberline Dock needs to show door occupancy clearly enough that the shift lead isn’t checking the camera monitor between every appointment.
- Door 6 was the useful example: a trailer can be physically in place while the sensor still reports the previous state. The team wants to see the last update time, not just an occupied/free label.
- We’ll start with sample sensor events from Tacoma, including a disconnect and a late-arriving update. Ops will pull these after the morning receiving rush.
- The overnight crew flagged that a blank status looks like an open door. Worth testing that display before anyone relies on it for scheduling.

## Next steps
- I’ll send the sample-event checklist and a short recap tomorow.
- Ops to confirm which Tacoma doors are in the first pass and send the feed field names.
- Set up a follow-up walkthrough once the samples arrive; keep it to 30 mins.

Order form targeted for end of May. Still need the Tacoma scope nailed down before that draft goes around.
